core_rule: Characters, settings, and events link to build theme. Change one part, change whole message.

hint_levels.template: How do person, place, and action work together to send message?
Find <character trait> and <setting detail>. Tell how <event> links them.
Story elements like gears; one turn moves others to create power.

worked_example.question: Shy girl enters loud, crowded stadium to give speech. What is meaning?
worked_example.answer: Growth happens when leaving comfort zones.

steps.instruction: Identify the character's main trait and the mood of the setting.
Analyse how the event forces the character to interact with that setting.
Combine these observations to state the overall message or theme.

worked_example.explanation: Character trait (shy) clashes with setting (loud). Event (speech) forces change. This creates theme of courage.

explanation_sections.heading: Narrative Meaning
explanation_sections.body: Stories use people, places, actions to show big ideas. Meaning is lesson or truth author shares.

explanation_sections.heading: Link Elements
explanation_sections.body: 1. Find character trait. 2. See how setting affects them. 3. Watch how event changes world. Link all three.

explanation_sections.heading: Model Text
explanation_sections.body: 'Aki held ancient scroll as temple bells rang.' Analysis: Aki (respectful) + Temple (tradition) + Bells (call to action) = Theme of duty.

explanation_sections.heading: Pitfall: Listing
explanation_sections.body: Do not just list facts. Link them. 'It is cold' is fact. 'Cold wind chilled his hope' is meaning.

common_mistakes: Ignoring how setting changes character mood

additional_worked_examples.question: Monkey King trapped under mountain for 500 years. Meaning?
additional_worked_examples.answer: Actions have long consequences; patience brings change.

steps.instruction: Identify the character's status at the start of the story.
Link the setting's constraints to the event's duration.
steps.result: Mountain is prison for long time.
